reads.monthly_note:
March was the household's tightest month. A $1,505 Lake Trust lump-sum loan payment — the largest single non-mortgage outflow in any statement — drove the deficit. Two failed mortgage auto-drafts from an underfunded secondary savings added $66 in overdraft fees.

The investment pipeline didn't pause: $1,300 flowed to Schwab and RH Brokerage on schedule. But liquidity thinned from $4,611 to $3,151, and the mortgage funding process showed a structural vulnerability — the secondary savings needs pre-funding before the auto-draft date.

The lump payment reduced outstanding debt, so the deficit isn't pure consumption. But the combination of debt paydown, investment transfers, and overdraft fees in a single month with $8,573 income pushed the household firmly into deficit territory.
